skill.name: otel-expert
skill.description: Answer OpenTelemetry questions using bundled documentation for semantic conventions, collector configuration, .NET instrumentation, OTLP, metrics, logs, traces, and spans.
skill.summary: Provides sourced OpenTelemetry guidance from bundled docs for instrumentation and observability work.
skill.author: ANcpLua

security_audit.summary: The six static findings are false positives caused by Markdown inline code and a fenced Grep example in SKILL.md. The skill only declares Read, Grep, and Glob tools and does not instruct shell execution, network access, or secret handling. No semantic prompt-injection or malicious intent was found.

static_findings.snippet: You have access to bundled OTel documentation at `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/docs/`.

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 9 uses Markdown inline code to show a documentation path variable. It does not execute a shell command or pass user input to a command interpreter.
Line 21 uses Markdown inline code for a relative documentation directory. This is a static path reference, not a command execution instruction.
Line 22 uses Markdown inline code for the collector documentation directory. No executable command or unsafe interpolation is present.
Line 23 uses Markdown inline code for a .NET instrumentation documentation file. It is a file reference, not shell backtick execution.
Line 24 uses Markdown inline code for a protocol documentation directory. The text does not invoke external commands.
The fenced bash block shows Grep tool examples against bundled documentation paths. The skill allows Read, Grep, and Glob only, with no shell execution or command injection path.

content.value_statement: OpenTelemetry work often requires exact semantic conventions and configuration details. This skill searches bundled OTel documentation and returns sourced guidance for instrumentation, collector setup, and OTLP decisions.
actual_capabilities: Finds OpenTelemetry topics by checking the bundled documentation index first.
Searches semantic convention, collector, protocol, and .NET instrumentation docs.
Returns source references for answers drawn from bundled files.
Highlights validation warnings from SYNC-REPORT.md when present.
Prioritizes latest stable semantic conventions and .NET 10 patterns.
limitations: It depends on the bundled documentation and may not include changes after the last sync.
It assumes OTLP export and avoids vendor-specific exporter guidance.
It does not run services, deploy collectors, or validate live telemetry pipelines.
It focuses on OpenTelemetry topics and is not a general observability strategy tool.

use_cases.title: Select Span Attributes
use_cases.description: Find the correct semantic convention attributes for traces, spans, metrics, logs, and resource metadata.

use_cases.title: Configure Collectors
use_cases.description: Locate collector receiver, processor, and exporter guidance for OTLP-based telemetry pipelines.

use_cases.title: Modernize .NET Telemetry
use_cases.description: Apply .NET 10 instrumentation patterns using ActivitySource, Meter, Logger, and OpenTelemetry guidance.

prompt_templates.title: Find an Attribute
prompt_templates.prompt: Find the latest stable OpenTelemetry semantic convention for this attribute need: [describe signal and entity]. Cite the source file.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Collector Settings
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the bundled collector docs and recommend receivers, processors, and exporters for this OTLP pipeline: [describe pipeline]. Mention source files.

prompt_templates.title: Review .NET Instrumentation
prompt_templates.prompt: Check this .NET telemetry approach against the bundled .NET instrumentation docs: [describe approach]. Identify outdated patterns and replacements.

prompt_templates.title: Resolve Cross-Signal Design
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare trace, metric, and log guidance for this OpenTelemetry design: [describe service]. Recommend stable attributes and cite each source.

output_examples.input: Which attributes should describe an HTTP client span?
output_examples.output: A concise table of stable HTTP span attributes, required status details, and source references from semantic convention docs.

output_examples.input: How should I configure an OTLP collector pipeline?
output_examples.output: A receiver, processor, and exporter recommendation with notes about defaults, warnings, and collector documentation sources.
A review that flags legacy patterns, recommends .NET 10 alternatives, and cites bundled instrumentation guidance.

best_practices: Ask for the signal type, runtime, and telemetry goal before requesting detailed guidance.
Request source file citations when using recommendations in production changes.
Check SYNC-REPORT.md warnings before relying on generated documentation content.
anti_patterns: Do not use it as proof that a live collector configuration has been tested.
Do not ask for vendor-specific exporter decisions when OTLP guidance is required.
Do not rely on deprecated attributes when the skill is constrained to latest stable conventions.

faq.question: What OpenTelemetry areas does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers semantic conventions, collector configuration, .NET instrumentation, OTLP, traces, spans, metrics, and logs.

faq.question: Does it cite sources?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill instructs the assistant to cite the bundled documentation file used for each answer.

faq.question: Can it validate a running collector?
faq.answer: No. It provides documentation-based guidance and does not inspect live systems or run collector tests.

faq.question: Does it support vendor exporters?
faq.answer: No. The skill assumes OTLP export and avoids vendor-specific exporter guidance.

faq.question: Is it useful for .NET services?
faq.answer: Yes. It prioritizes .NET 10 instrumentation patterns and related bundled documentation.

faq.question: How current is the guidance?
faq.answer: It depends on the bundled documentation. Check SYNC-REPORT.md warnings when freshness matters.
